items.title: Two Closing Verses Seal the Teaching on Pervasive Objects

items.zh: 頡隸伐多！為此比丘於所緣境安住其心，如是於緣安住其心，如是於緣安住心已，名善安住。世尊此中重說頌曰：行者行諸相，知一切實義，常於影靜慮，得證遍清淨。此中說言「行者行諸相」者，由此宣說修觀行者，於止、舉、捨相，無間修行、殷重修行。若復說言：知一切實義者。由此宣說事邊際性。若復說言：常於影靜慮者。由此宣說有分別影像、無分別影像。若復說言：得證遍清淨者。由此宣說所作成辦。此中世尊復說頌曰：於心相遍知，能受遠離味。靜慮常委念，受喜樂離染。此中說言「於心相遍知」者，謂有分別影像、無分別影像，以心相名說；事邊際性，以遍知名說。若復說言：能受遠離味者。由此宣說於其所緣正修行者樂斷樂修。若復說言：靜慮常委念者。由此宣說於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，常勤修習、委練修習。若復說言：受喜樂離染者。由此宣說所作成辦。當知如是遍滿所緣，隨順淨教，契合正理。
items.en: Revata! It is in this way that a monk settles the mind on the object, settles the mind on it correctly, and, having settled the mind this way, is said to be genuinely well settled. The Blessed One then spoke this verse: "The practitioner engages every mark, knows the true meaning of all things, constantly absorbed in the image, attains universal purity." … The Blessed One spoke a further verse: "Fully knowing the mind's own mark, tasting the flavour of genuine release, ever absorbed with careful mindfulness, one receives joy and freedom from defilement." … Know that these pervasive objects accord with the pure teaching and are in keeping with correct principle.

items.title: Section: Purifying Objects Reopen in Full — Six Kinds of Impurity, and the Body's Thirty-Six Parts

items.zh: 如是名為遍滿所緣。云何名為淨行所緣？謂不淨、慈愍、緣性緣起、界差別、阿那波那念等所緣差別。云何不淨所緣？謂略說有六種不淨。一、朽穢不淨，二、苦惱不淨，三、下劣不淨，四、觀待不淨，五、煩惱不淨，六、速壞不淨。云何名為朽穢不淨？謂此不淨，略依二種。一者、依內，二者、依外。云何依內朽穢不淨？謂內身中，髮、毛、爪、齒、塵、垢、皮、肉、骸、骨、筋、脈、心、膽、肝、肺、大腸、小腸、生藏、熟藏、肚、胃、脾、腎、膿、血、熱痰、肪、膏、肌、髓、腦、膜、洟、唾、淚、汗、屎、尿。
items.en: This is called pervasive objects. What are purifying objects? They comprise the distinct objects of impurity, loving-kindness, dependent origination, analysis of the elements, and mindfulness of breathing. What is the object of impurity? Briefly, there are six kinds: decaying impurity, the impurity of suffering, base impurity, comparative impurity, afflictive impurity, and the impurity of swift decay. What is decaying impurity? Briefly, it depends on two things: what is internal, and what is external. What is internal decaying impurity? Within the body: hair, body hair, nails, teeth, grime, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, blood vessels, heart, gallbladder, liver, lungs, large intestine, small intestine, the receptacle of undigested food and that of digested food [such as the stomach and the small intestine], the abdomen, the stomach itself, spleen, kidneys, pus and blood, phlegm, fat, grease, muscle, marrow, brain, membrane, mucus, saliva, tears, sweat, feces, and urine.

items.zh: 如是等類，名為依內朽穢不淨。

items.title: Section: External Decay, and Four More Kinds of Impurity

items.zh: 云何依外朽穢不淨？謂或青瘀、或復膿爛、或復變壞、或復膖脹、或復食噉、或復變赤、或復散壞、或骨、或鎖、或復骨鎖、或屎所作、或尿所作、或唾所作、或洟所作、或血所塗、或膿所塗、或便穢處。如是等類，名為依外朽穢不淨。如是依內朽穢不淨及依外朽穢不淨，總說為一朽穢不淨。云何名為苦惱不淨？謂順苦受觸為緣所生，若身、若心不平等受，受所攝。如是名為苦惱不淨。云何名為下劣不淨？謂最下劣事、最下劣界，所謂欲界。除此更無極下、極劣、最極鄙穢餘界可得。如是名為下劣不淨。云何名為觀待不淨？謂如有一劣清淨事，觀待其餘勝清淨事，便似不淨。如待無色勝清淨事，色界諸法便似不淨；待薩迦耶寂滅涅槃，乃至有頂皆似不淨。
items.en: What is external decaying impurity? A corpse turning livid, or festering, or decomposing, or bloating, or being devoured, or discolored with blood, or scattered apart, reduced to bone, or bone held by sinew, or a skeleton of linked bones … Internal and external decaying impurity together are called, as one, decaying impurity. What is the impurity of suffering? Painful feeling arising from painful contact, whether of body or mind, together with whatever accompanies that feeling. What is base impurity? The most inferior condition, the most inferior realm — namely, the desire realm. … What is comparative impurity? It is when an inferior state of purity, set against a superior one, comes to seem impure by comparison — form-realm phenomena appearing impure next to the formless realm's superior purity, and every realm up to the very peak of existence appearing impure next to the peace of nirvana itself.

items.zh: 如是等類，一切名為觀待不淨。

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Impurity Close; Five Kinds of Craving Open

items.zh: 云何名為煩惱不淨？謂三界中，所有一切結、縛、隨眠、隨煩惱、纏，一切名為煩惱不淨。云何名為速壞不淨？謂五取蘊，無常、無恒、不可保信、變壞法性。如是名為速壞不淨。如是不淨，是能清淨貪行所緣？貪有五種。一、於內身欲欲欲貪，二、於外身婬欲婬貪，三、境欲境貪，四、色欲色貪，五、薩迦耶欲薩迦耶貪。是名五貪。為欲令此五種欲貪斷滅、除遣、不現行故，建立六種不淨所緣。謂由依內朽穢不淨所緣故，令於內身欲欲欲貪，心得清淨。由依外朽穢不淨所緣故，令於外身婬欲婬貪，心得清淨。婬相應貪復有四種。一、顯色貪，二、形色貪，三、妙觸貪，四、承事貪。
items.en: What is afflictive impurity? All the fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, secondary afflictions, and entanglements throughout the three realms — all of this is called afflictive impurity. What is the impurity of swift decay? The five aggregates of grasping — impermanent, unstable, unreliable, and subject by nature to decay. … Such impurities purify the object connected with desire-type conduct. Desire is of five kinds: craving for one's own body, lustful craving for another's body, craving for sense-objects, craving for form-realm absorption, and craving rooted in self-view. These are the five cravings. … Through the object of internal decaying impurity, craving for one's own body is purified in the mind. Through the object of external decaying impurity, lustful craving for another's body is purified in the mind. Lust-connected craving is itself of four kinds: craving for complexion, craving for physique, craving for pleasing touch, and craving for being served.

items.zh: 由依四外不淨所緣，於此四種相應婬貪，心得清淨。若於青瘀、或於膿爛、或於變壞、或於膖脹、或於食噉作意思惟，於顯色貪令心清淨。

blocks.text: After two verses that close the Revata dialogue, the treatise explains the first **purifying object**: impurity.
"Revata, it is in this way that a monk settles the mind on the object, settles it correctly, and is genuinely well settled." The Buddha's verses conclude the teaching on the pervasive objects.
Impurity, loving-kindness, dependent origination, analysis of the elements, and mindfulness of breathing: one for each temperament (Day 225).

items: **Decaying impurity**: internal, the thirty-six parts of the body: "hair, body hair, nails, teeth… faeces, and urine". Master Cháng Bǎi: most people rarely think that this is what they are. External: a corpse turning livid, festering, bloating, devoured, scattered, reduced to bones.
**Base impurity**: "the most inferior realm, the desire realm". Master Cháng Bǎi: it has the most suffering.
**Comparative impurity**: the form realm is impure compared with the formless, and "every realm up to the peak of existence appears impure next to the peace of nirvāṇa".
**Afflictive impurity**: all fetters, bonds, and latent tendencies.
**Impurity of swift decay**: all conditioned things perish quickly.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: internal impurity is while one is alive; external, after death.

Craving for one's own body; lustful craving for another's body; craving for sense objects; craving for form-realm absorption; craving for identity. Lust has four forms: craving for complexion, physique, pleasing touch, and being served.

"Impurity" (aśubha) is not a moral judgement about the body. It is a deliberate counterweight to the habit of seeing the body, or anything, as purely lovely. Master Cháng Bǎi warned (Day 178) that it suits some temperaments and not others.

quiz.q: What are the six kinds of impurity, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi advise meditators?
options: decaying, suffering, base, comparative, afflictive, swift-decay; memorise the passage on the body's thirty-six parts as a meditation object
quiz.why: "Decaying impurity, the impurity of suffering, base impurity, comparative impurity, afflictive impurity, and the impurity of swift decay." Master Cháng Bǎi: meditators should memorise this passage and use it as the object in sitting.

quiz.q: Internal decaying impurity lists hair through urine. How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the body?
options: a walking latrine, holding feces, urine, and sweat
quiz.why: "Within the body: hair, body hair, nails, teeth … feces, and urine." Master Cháng Bǎi: most beings rarely think that their body is a walking latrine, full of feces, urine, and sweat.

quiz.q: Decaying impurity is internal or external. How do the masters divide them?
options: Miào Jìng: internal is while living, external at death; Cháng Bǎi: a corpse is no longer held by the storehouse consciousness, hence "external"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: internal impurity is while one is alive; external, at death. Master Cháng Bǎi: after death the body becomes a corpse no longer held by the storehouse consciousness — hence "external."

quiz.q: What does "base impurity" refer to, and why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the desire realm, where all ten unwholesome deeds are present
quiz.why: "The most inferior condition, the most inferior realm — namely, the desire realm." Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire realm has all ten unwholesome deeds, so it is base impurity.

quiz.q: Next to nirvāṇa, even the peak of existence seems impure. Why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, is the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception impure?
options: the noble path is not attained there; beings are still ordinary, still in the round of birth and death
quiz.why: "Every realm up to the very peak of existence appearing impure next to the peace of nirvana itself." Master Cháng Bǎi: beings in that sphere have not attained the noble path; they are still ordinary, still turning in birth and death — so it too is impure.

quiz.q: Afflictive impurity pervades the three realms. Does Venerable Miào Jìng say attaining concentration makes one pure?
options: attaining concentration without the foundations of mindfulness is still impure
quiz.why: "All the fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, secondary afflictions, and entanglements throughout the three realms — all of this is called afflictive impurity." Venerable Miào Jìng: in Buddhist terms, if you attain concentration without cultivating the foundations of mindfulness, that is still impure.
